findings.text: Range mapping service visible beyond its file. It divides a requested byte interval into large page friendly spans, builds direct mappings for each span with caller supplied protections, records covered frames in the global tracker, and reports progress as a frame count.

Boot time direct map initializer. It sequences mitigation checks and feature probing before mapping low and general memory, selects a direction aware strategy, installs the result as the active translation, and then invokes hypervisor and memory test hooks.

Thirty two bit constructor for kernel direct mappings over the swapper directory. It walks directory levels for the requested physical span, creates missing intermediate tables, selects large or small pages from caller hint and hardware ability, treats kernel text with execution permission, and returns the mapping frontier.
Sixty four bit front for physical mapping. It forwards interval bounds with size hint and protections to a shared low level initializer that creates entries, returning that helper result.

Boot policy hook for kernel page table isolation. It examines hypervisor kind with command mode plus attack vector state and vulnerability presence to decide enablement, and clears conflicting processor abilities when isolation stays on.

Trampoline table builder for randomized memory layout. It allocates low table pages, mirrors the existing low megabyte direct entry into an identity indexed slot, and publishes a top level trampoline entry compatible with both paging depths.
Thirty two bit setup for the fixed address window backing early input output remapping. It ensures table pages exist across the fixed span and then resets early remap state.

Single boot entry establishing the kernel direct map. It assumes firmware memory topology is known, always maps the low compatibility hole, then maps remaining memory directionally before switching address spaces and flushing translation caches.

Repeatable mapping entry for arbitrary physical spans during boot. Callers provide start with end and protections and receive the mapped extent as a frame number while global mapped interval state is updated.

Boot mapping descriptor holding a byte start with a byte end plus a mask of permissible large page sizes for that span. Splitting fills an array of such descriptors and merging preserves contiguity with equal masks.
Processor vulnerability table pairing model identities with minimum acceptable microcode levels. Each valid row names one affected family and its safety floor, followed by an empty terminator row.

Global record of mapped frame intervals using an array sized by firmware table limits with a live entry count. Entries stay merged and ordered and two high water marks track total mapped frames and low mapped frames.

Process context identifier support activates only on sixty four bit when the boot processor advertises it and, for listed vulnerable models, only when microcode reaches the model floor. Global page support is also required, otherwise the feature is cleared. The control register bit is set directly to accommodate secondary boot handling.

Range recording ignores empty intervals and aborts boot when the static array is full. Valid intervals are stored as byte addresses derived from frame numbers with the supplied size mask, advancing the valid count by one.

Interval splitting prefers large pages for aligned middles while keeping unaligned head and tail on small pages. Thirty two bit keeps the opening table block small, sixty four bit adds a gigabyte aligned middle, masks are upgraded before allocator handover, neighbors with shared mask and contiguity merge, and each final span is logged.

A span gains a larger size only when global permission allows it and the span expanded outward to that size lies wholly in usable memory. Thirty two bit skips medium upgrades whose expanded end leaves low memory.
Span label shows the largest allowed size with gigabyte first then megabyte then kilobyte. Legacy thirty two bit without address extension names the medium size as four megabytes.

Thirty two bit mapping installs identity attributes first with chosen page sizes, flushes translation caches, then rewrites final kernel protections without altering size and frame together. Usage counters update only during the first sweep.
Kernel text membership holds exactly for addresses from text start through initialization end inclusive. All other addresses count as non text for permission selection.

Chunk handling intersects firmware memory frame intervals with the requested byte window and maps non empty intersections with standard kernel protections. Use of the boot reserved table area is suspended for chunks overlapping it and restored afterward.

Mapping advances in chunks beginning at two megabytes and growing geometrically after mapped volume catches the current step. Top down begins near the end after reserving a top block, while bottom up begins at the base and moves upward.

Sixty four bit trampoline setup copies the live top entry for the direct map slot when memory randomization is off, otherwise it builds fresh low tables mirroring the low megabyte entry and publishes a new top entry with kernel table rights.

Boot mapping maps the low compatibility hole first, then remaining memory in two phases around the kernel image when allocation grows upward or in one top down sweep otherwise. Sixty four bit promotes the low limit when high memory exists, then loads the new top directory, flushes caches, and calls hypervisor plus test hooks.

Fixed window preparation counts only directory slots overlapping the high memory temporary window, preallocates that many pages, creates missing levels across the window, and relocates any early nonlinear temporary pages into the reserved area.

Isolation stays off under paravirtual Xen and when automatic mode finds the user kernel vector unmitigated, plus automatic mode exits quietly without the Meltdown defect. Forced modes are logged when active, and enabling isolation disables broadcast invalidate with fast exception delivery.
Mapped interval insertion merges the new span with existing entries, restores sorted order, and raises total and low high water marks with low mark capped to the thirty two bit boundary.
Thirty two bit mapping moves from initial install to permission tightening with a mandatory global flush between. Counting happens solely in the initial state and return follows the tightening sweep.

Isolation mode begins automatic or forced. Automatic can decay to forced off from environment checks, while surviving automatic with vulnerability and any forced on path converge to enabled with conflicts cleared.

Table page sourcing alternates per chunk between boot reserved storage and block allocator storage based on overlap with the reserved window, always returning to boot reserved storage after each chunk.
Exceeding the small static descriptor capacity during splitting aborts boot, so partitioning must remain within three to five spans depending on build.

Process identifiers without global page support would invalidate the global flush routine, so the pair is refused to avoid corruption on misconfigured virtual machines even though no real hardware presents it.
Aliasing kernel tables into the user half with the global flag means trampoline use creates global entries, which reviewers must weigh for isolation and flushing.
Changing page size together with frame or attributes in one store violates translation cache guidance, avoided here by separating size establishment from permission finalization with a flush between.

Temporary mapping tables must remain linear across the reserved window. Nonlinearity from early fixmap use requires relocation into preallocated pages, and residual gaps or late use trigger fatal checks.

Many reserved holes near the top can exhaust boot table space with small pages. The top down path reserves a large aligned block first and falls back to a truncated start with a warning when reservation fails.
Boot split capacity is three spans in one build variant and five spans in the other variant.
Flush correct microcode floor for Alder Lake is 0x2e.
Flush correct microcode floor for Alder Lake L is 0x42c.
Flush correct microcode floor for Gracemont Atom is 0x11.
Flush correct microcode floor for Raptor Lake is 0x118.
Flush correct microcode floor for Raptor Lake P is 0x4117.
Flush correct microcode floor for Raptor Lake S is 0x2e.
Displayed granularity names are 1G with 2M plus 4M on legacy non extended thirty two bit and 4k as default.
Mapped frame interval storage holds as many entries as the firmware memory map entry limit.
